\chapter{Learning Theory — Convex Minimax Separation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Minimax.ConvexMinimaxSeparation
\section{Overview}

This module proves the convex-compact minimax theorem by a Hahn--Banach separation
route. For each finite sample $u$ of columns it forms the \emph{upper image} of the
payoff on that sample, separates the constant vector $(v+\varepsilon,\dots,v+\varepsilon)$ from it
by a continuous linear functional, and normalizes the coordinates of that functional
into a mixed column strategy. This yields the finite sublevel intersection property,
which combined with compactness of the row set gives the minimax identity
$\inf_{x} \sup_{y} f(x,y) = \sup_{y} \inf_{x} f(x,y)$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Finite upper image of the payoff]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}
\leanok
For sets $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, a payoff $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$, and a finite
sample $u$ of columns from $Y$, the finite upper image is the set
\[
  U(X,f,u) \;=\; \{\, z : u \to \bbr \;\mid\; \exists\, x \in X,\ \forall y \in u,\ f(x,y) < z_y \,\}
\]
of vectors that strictly dominate the payoff vector of some row on the sample $u$.
This set is written $\texttt{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}$ in Lean.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonemptiness of the finite upper image]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_nonempty}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_nonempty}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}
\difficulty{2}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and
let $u$ be a finite sample of columns from $Y$. If $X$ is nonempty, then the finite
upper image $U(X,f,u)$ is nonempty; that is, there exists a vector $z : u \to \bbr$ for
which some $x \in X$ satisfies $f(x,y) < z_y$ for every $y \in u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Convexity of the finite upper image]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_convex}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_convex}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff, and let $u$ be
a finite sample of columns from $Y$. If $X$ is convex and, for every $y \in Y$, the map
$x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is convex on $X$, then the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$ is a convex
subset of $u \to \bbr$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Finite upper image is upward closed]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_upper}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_upper}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff, and let $u$ be
a finite sample of columns from $Y$. If a vector $z : u \to \bbr$ belongs to the finite
upper image $U(X,f,u)$, and $z' : u \to \bbr$ satisfies $z_y \le z'_y$ for every $y \in
u$, then $z'$ also belongs to $U(X,f,u)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The finite upper image is open]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_isOpen}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_isOpen}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and
let $u$ be a finite sample of columns from $Y$. Then the finite upper image
\[
U(X,f,u) \;=\; \{\, z : u \to \bbr \;\mid\; \exists\, x \in X,\ \forall y \in u,\ f(x,y)
< z_y \,\}
\]
is an open subset of the space $u \to \bbr$ of vectors indexed by $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coordinate expansion of a continuous linear functional]
\lean{OnlineLearning.continuousLinearMap_pi_apply_eq_sum_single}
\label{OnlineLearning.continuousLinearMap_pi_apply_eq_sum_single}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set and let $L \colon \bbr^{\iota} \to \bbr$ be a
continuous linear functional. Writing $e_i$ for the standard basis vector whose $i$-th
coordinate is $1$ and whose other coordinates are $0$, every vector $z \in \bbr^{\iota}$
satisfies
\[
  L(z) \;=\; \sum_{i \in \iota} z_i \, L(e_i).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Separating functional is coordinatewise nonpositive]
\lean{OnlineLearning.separating_coordinate_nonpos}
\label{OnlineLearning.separating_coordinate_nonpos}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_nonempty, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_upper}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff, let $u$ be a
finite sample of columns from $Y$, and let $c : u \to \bbr$ be a fixed vector. Suppose
$X$ is nonempty and $L : (u \to \bbr) \to \bbr$ is a continuous linear functional such
that $L(z) < L(c)$ for every $z$ in the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$. Then for each
coordinate $y \in u$ one has $L(e_y) \le 0$, where $e_y \in (u \to \bbr)$ is the
standard basis vector taking the value $1$ at $y$ and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A nonzero separating functional over the upper image]
\lean{OnlineLearning.separating_functional_ne_zero}
\label{OnlineLearning.separating_functional_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_nonempty}
\difficulty{2}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff, and let $u$ be
a finite sample of columns drawn from $Y$, with $X$ nonempty. Fix a vector $c : u \to
\bbr$ and a continuous linear functional $L : (u \to \bbr) \to \bbr$. If $L(z) < L(c)$
for every $z$ in the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$, then $L$ is not the zero functional.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positivity of the separator's total weight]
\lean{OnlineLearning.separating_weight_sum_pos}
\label{OnlineLearning.separating_weight_sum_pos}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.continuousLinearMap_pi_apply_eq_sum_single, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage, OnlineLearning.separating_coordinate_nonpos, OnlineLearning.separating_functional_ne_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and
let $u$ be a finite sample of columns drawn from $Y$. Suppose $X$ is nonempty, fix a
vector $c \in \bbr^u$, and let $L : \bbr^u \to \bbr$ be a continuous linear functional
that strictly separates $c$ from the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$, in the sense that
$L(z) < L(c)$ for every $z \in U(X,f,u)$. Writing $e_y \in \bbr^u$ for the standard
basis vector supported at coordinate $y$, one then has
\[
  0 \;<\; \sum_{y \in u} \bigl(-L(e_y)\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonempty finite intersection of minimax sublevel sets]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finite_sublevel_intersections_by_separation}
\label{OnlineLearning.finite_sublevel_intersections_by_separation}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.continuousLinearMap_pi_apply_eq_sum_single, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_convex, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperImage_isOpen, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel, OnlineLearning.separating_coordinate_nonpos, OnlineLearning.separating_weight_sum_pos}
\difficulty{7}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact
minimax hypotheses, and write $v = \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y)$ for the lower
value of the payoff. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every finite set $u$ of
columns chosen from $Y$, there is a row $x \in X$ with $f(x,y) \le v + \varepsilon$
simultaneously for all $y \in u$; equivalently, the intersection over $y \in u$ of the
sublevel sets $\{x \in X : f(x,y) \le v + \varepsilon\}$ is nonempty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Minimax equality from finite sublevel intersections]
\lean{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_of_finite_sublevel_intersections}
\label{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_of_finite_sublevel_intersections}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement, OnlineLearning.exists_forall_le_of_finite_sublevel_intersections, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel, OnlineLearning.weak_convex_compact_minimax}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ with $X$ and $Y$ nonempty, $X$ compact and convex, and $Y$
convex, and let $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ be bounded above and below on $X \times
Y$, with $f(\cdot, y)$ continuous and convex on $X$ for every $y \in Y$ and $f(x,
\cdot)$ concave on $Y$ for every $x \in X$. Write $v = \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X}
f(x,y)$ for the lower value, and suppose that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every
finite set $u$ of column points from $Y$, the set
\[
  \{x \in X : f(x,y) \leq v + \varepsilon \text{ for all } y \in u\}
\]
is nonempty. Then the minimax equality
\[
  \inf_{x \in X}\,\sup_{y \in Y}\,f(x,y) \;=\; \sup_{y \in Y}\,\inf_{x \in X}\,f(x,y)
\]
holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A convex–concave minimax equality]
\lean{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_by_separation}
\label{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_by_separation}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement, OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_of_finite_sublevel_intersections, OnlineLearning.finite_sublevel_intersections_by_separation}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ be nonempty sets with $X$ compact and both $X$ and $Y$ convex,
and let $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function that is bounded above and
below on $X \times Y$. Suppose that for every $y \in Y$ the section $x \mapsto f(x,y)$
is continuous and convex on $X$, while for every $x \in X$ the section $y \mapsto
f(x,y)$ is concave on $Y$. Then the minimax equality
\[
  \inf_{x \in X}\,\sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{y \in Y}\,\inf_{x \in X} f(x,y)
\]
holds.
\end{theorem}
